examples.en: The newlywed groom walked in carrying his bride.

examples.ko: 우리 오빠는 새신랑이라서 요즘 항상 일찍 퇴근해요.
examples.en: My brother is a newlywed, so he always leaves work early these days.
The groom looks really happy.
His friends played a prank on the groom.

examples.ko: 결혼식 날 새신랑은 너무 긴장해서 말을 더듬었어요.
examples.en: On the wedding day, the groom was so nervous that he stammered.

examples.ko: 새신랑과 새색시가 함께 어른들께 인사를 드렸어요.
examples.en: The groom and the bride greeted the elders together.

explain: 결혼한 지 얼마 안 된 남자를 말할 때 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '새색시'나 '새신부'예요. 결혼식 날의 남자는 그냥 '신랑'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for a man who has only recently married. Its counterparts are '새색시' and '새신부'. The man on the wedding day can also simply be called '신랑'.

examples.ko: 저는 열 살 때 새어머니를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my stepmother when I was ten.
My stepmother cares for me like her own daughter.
My stepmother made me a delicious kimchi stew.
At first, talking with my stepmother felt awkward.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 새어머니가 나쁜 사람으로 나올 때가 많아요.
examples.en: In dramas, the stepmother is often shown as a bad person.
On Parents' Day this time, I gave flowers to my stepmother.

explain: '계모'라는 말도 있지만 부정적인 느낌이 강해서, 말할 때나 부를 때는 '새어머니'가 부드러워요. 아버지 쪽은 '새아버지'라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '어머니'나 '엄마'라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: There is also the word '계모', but it carries a strong negative feeling, so '새어머니' is gentler when talking about her. The father's side is '새아버지'. When addressing her directly, people often just say '어머니' or '엄마'.

examples.ko: 새언니가 저한테 예쁜 가방을 선물해 줬어요.
examples.en: My brother's wife gave me a pretty bag as a present.
My sister-in-law is really good at cooking.

examples.ko: 새언니, 이번 주말에 우리 집에 오실 거예요?
examples.en: Sister-in-law, will you come to our house this weekend?
My brother and his wife got married last year.
I get along very well with my sister-in-law.
I bought baby clothes for my sister-in-law.

explain: 오빠의 아내를 여동생이 부르거나 가리키는 말이에요. 남동생이 형의 아내를 부를 때는 '형수님'이라고 해요. 호칭으로도 그대로 써서 '새언니'라고 부르면 돼요.
explain_en: A younger sister uses this for her older brother's wife. A younger brother calls his older brother's wife '형수님' instead. It also works directly as a form of address: you can just call her '새언니'.

en: cut in line; jump in line

examples.ko: 줄을 서지 않고 새치기하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut in line without waiting your turn.

examples.ko: 어떤 아저씨가 제 앞으로 새치기해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: A man cut in front of me and I got angry.

examples.ko: 새치기하지 마세요. 뒤에 사람들이 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: Please don't cut in line. People are waiting behind you.

examples.ko: 매점에서 새치기한 사람을 보고 친구가 한마디 했어요.
examples.en: My friend said something to the person who cut in line at the snack bar.
The kids got scolded by the teacher for cutting in line.

examples.ko: 버스를 탈 때 새치기하는 사람은 정말 얄미워요.
examples.en: People who cut in line when boarding a bus are really annoying.

explain: 줄이나 순서를 지키지 않고 앞에 끼어드는 행동에 써요. 운전할 때 차선에 끼어드는 건 보통 '끼어들다'라고 해요. '새치기'는 명사로도 많이 써서 '새치기 금지'처럼 붙여요.
explain_en: It is used when someone ignores a line or order and pushes in front. For cars merging into a lane, people usually say '끼어들다'. '새치기' is also often used as a noun, as in '새치기 금지' (no cutting in line).

en: pitch-dark; as black as a crow; as black as soot

examples.ko: 하늘이 새카매서 별이 아주 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The sky is pitch-dark, so the stars are very clear.
After playing outside, my face turned really dark.

examples.ko: 정전이 되자 방 안이 온통 새카맸어요.
examples.en: When the power went out, the whole room was pitch-black.
The meat burned and turned black as soot.
The child's eyes are jet-black and round.
Pitch-black clouds rolled in and the rain poured down.

explain: '까맣다'보다 훨씬 진하게 까만 느낌이에요. 'ㅎ'이 빠지는 불규칙이라서 '새카매요, 새카만, 새카맸어요'로 바뀌어요. '새까맣다'라고도 하는데 느낌이 조금 더 세요.
explain_en: It feels much deeper black than '까맣다'. It is an irregular 'ㅎ' adjective, so it becomes '새카매요', '새카만', '새카맸어요'. You may also hear '새까맣다', which feels a bit stronger.

examples.ko: 탕수육 소스가 새콤달콤해서 계속 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: The sweet and sour pork sauce is so tasty that I keep eating.
I want to eat sweet and sour spicy noodles.
This strawberry jam is sweet and tangy and smells good too.
I think I made the sauce too sweet and sour.
My mom made me a sweet and sour cucumber salad.
The tangerines are sweeter and tangier than expected, so the kids like them.

explain: '새콤'은 기분 좋은 가벼운 신맛이라서 좋은 맛을 말할 때 써요. 상해서 시큼한 맛과는 느낌이 달라요. 과일, 소스, 무침처럼 맛있는 음식에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '새콤' is a light, pleasant sourness, so it is used for tastes people enjoy. It feels different from the sharp sourness of food that has gone off. It fits tasty things like fruit, sauces and seasoned side dishes.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 해마다 새해맞이 여행을 가요.
examples.en: My family goes on a New Year trip every year.
They handed out tteokguk at the New Year event.

examples.ko: 새해맞이를 위해 집 안 대청소를 했어요.
examples.en: We did a big house cleaning to welcome the new year.
We watched the sunrise at the beach to welcome the new year.
Are you all done getting ready for the new year?
I sent New Year greetings to my friends by text.

explain: 새해를 맞는 준비나 행사, 여행을 말할 때 써요. 한국에서는 새해 첫날 일출을 보러 가는 것을 '해돋이'라고 하는데, 이것도 새해맞이의 하나예요. 인사말은 '새해 복 많이 받으세요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for the preparations, events or trips for welcoming the new year. In Korea, going to watch the first sunrise of the year is called '해돋이', which is one kind of 새해맞이. The greeting is '새해 복 많이 받으세요'.

examples.en: The forsythia has bloomed bright yellow.
Bright yellow chicks are wandering around the yard.
The ginkgo leaves are vivid yellow, so it feels like autumn.

examples.ko: 아이의 가방이 샛노랗고 아주 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The child's bag is bright yellow and really stands out.
The ginkgo trees in autumn color were completely golden yellow.

examples.ko: 바나나가 아직 샛노랗지 않고 초록빛이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The bananas aren't bright yellow yet and still have some green.

explain: '노랗다'보다 훨씬 짙고 선명한 노란색이에요. '새빨갛다, 새파랗다'처럼 색을 강조하는 말이에요. 'ㅎ'이 빠지는 불규칙이라서 '샛노래요, 샛노란'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is a much deeper, more vivid yellow than '노랗다'. Like '새빨갛다' and '새파랗다', it emphasizes the color. It is an irregular 'ㅎ' adjective, so it becomes '샛노래요' and '샛노란'.

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있을 때 생강차를 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink ginger tea when I feel like I'm catching a cold.
One cup of warm ginger tea, please.

examples.ko: 생강차는 꿀을 넣으면 맛이 더 부드러워요.
examples.en: Ginger tea tastes smoother if you add honey.
I warmed myself up with ginger tea on a cold day.
In winter, citron tea is good and ginger tea is good too.
This café is famous for its tasty ginger tea.

explain: '차'가 붙었지만 찻잎이 아니라 생강을 끓이거나 우려서 만든 음료예요. 한국에서는 '유자차, 대추차, 쌍화차'처럼 이런 전통차가 많아요. 감기에 걸렸을 때나 몸이 찰 때 찾는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: Although it ends in '차', it is not made from tea leaves but from ginger that is boiled or steeped. Korea has many traditional drinks like this, such as '유자차', '대추차' and '쌍화차'. Many people reach for it when they have a cold or feel chilly.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 매주 금요일 밤에 생방송해요.
examples.en: This program airs live every Friday night.
I heard they'll broadcast the prime minister's announcement live this evening.

examples.ko: 생방송하는 중에는 실수해도 다시 찍을 수 없어서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: During a live broadcast you can't redo a mistake, so I get nervous.
The singer broadcast the fan meeting live.
I wish they would broadcast the game live from start to finish.
The sound cut out while they were broadcasting the concert live yesterday.

explain: 보통은 '생방송'이라는 명사로 많이 말해서 '생방송으로 나와요', '생방송 중이에요'처럼 써요. 행사나 경기를 그대로 보여 줄 때는 '생중계하다'도 자주 써요. 반대는 미리 찍어 두는 '녹화방송'이에요.
explain_en: People more often use the noun '생방송', as in '생방송으로 나와요' or '생방송 중이에요'. For showing an event or game as it happens, '생중계하다' is also common. The opposite is '녹화방송', which is recorded in advance.

examples.ko: 아침에 어머니가 미역국으로 생일상을 차려 주셨어요.
examples.en: In the morning, my mother set a birthday table with seaweed soup for me.

examples.ko: 혼자 먹는 생일상이 쓸쓸해서 친구에게 전화를 걸었어요.
examples.en: Eating a birthday meal alone felt lonely, so I called a friend.

examples.ko: 할머니 생일상에는 잡채와 떡이 꼭 올라가요.
examples.en: Japchae and rice cakes always go on Grandma's birthday table.

examples.ko: 생일상 앞에서 가족이 노래를 불러 줬어요.
examples.en: My family sang to me in front of the birthday table.
I was touched by the birthday meal my husband made himself.
Please keep this year's birthday meal simple.

explain: 생일에 차리는 음식 한 상을 말해요. 한국에서는 미역국이 생일 음식의 대표라서 생일상에 자주 올라가요. 보통 '생일상을 차리다, 생일상을 받다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means the spread of food prepared for a birthday. Seaweed soup is the classic Korean birthday dish, so it often appears on the table. People usually say '생일상을 차리다' (to set it) and '생일상을 받다' (to be served one).

examples.en: The fresh cream cake is soft and delicious.
Please put whipped cream on top of the coffee.
Please keep the fresh cream in the refrigerator.
The cream was too sweet, so I only ate a little.
Even just the cream by itself is rich and tasty.

examples.ko: 생크림과 우유는 비슷해 보여도 쓰임이 달라요.
examples.en: Fresh cream and milk look similar, but they are used differently.

explain: 우유에서 얻은 크림으로, 케이크나 빵집 메뉴에서 '생크림 케이크'처럼 자주 보여요. 거품을 낸 크림을 '휘핑크림'이라고도 해요. 영어 whipped cream과 완전히 같지는 않아서, 거품 내기 전의 크림도 생크림이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is cream made from milk and often appears on bakery menus as '생크림 케이크'. Cream that has been whipped is also called '휘핑크림'. It is not exactly the same as English 'whipped cream', because the cream before whipping is also called 생크림.

examples.en: I folded the clothes and put them in the dresser.

examples.ko: 문구류는 따로 신청하지 말고 서랍장에서 필요한 만큼 가져가세요.
examples.en: Don't request stationery separately; take what you need from the drawer chest.

examples.ko: 방이 좁아서 서랍장을 놓을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: The room is small, so there's no space to put a chest of drawers.

examples.ko: 서랍장 맨 아래 칸이 잘 안 열려요.
examples.en: The bottom drawer of the chest won't open easily.
I heard the new chest of drawers is being delivered today.

examples.ko: 이 서랍장은 칸이 다섯 개나 돼서 편해요.
examples.en: This chest has as many as five drawers, so it's convenient.

explain: '서랍'은 열고 닫는 칸 하나를 말하고, '서랍장'은 그런 칸이 여러 개 있는 가구예요. 옷을 걸어 두는 '옷장'과 달리 접은 옷이나 작은 물건을 넣어요. 칸을 셀 때는 '칸'이나 '단'으로 말해요.
explain_en: '서랍' is a single sliding drawer, while '서랍장' is the piece of furniture with several of them. Unlike a '옷장' where you hang clothes, you keep folded clothes and small items in it. You count the drawers with '칸' or '단'.

examples.ko: 부산에서 온 친구가 서울말을 쓰려고 노력해요.
examples.en: My friend from Busan is trying to speak the Seoul way.

examples.ko: 서울말과 부산 사투리의 차이를 이제는 구별할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can now tell the difference between Seoul speech and the Busan dialect.
If you watch dramas, your Seoul-style speech improves naturally.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 서울말도 잘하고 사투리도 잘해요.
examples.en: That actor is good at both Seoul speech and dialects.
The Seoul accent was unfamiliar, so it was hard at first.

examples.ko: 표준어는 교양 있는 사람들이 두루 쓰는 현대 서울말로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The standard language is defined as the modern Seoul speech widely used by educated people.

explain: 서울 지역에서 쓰는 말이에요. 표준어는 서울말을 바탕으로 정해졌지만 둘이 똑같은 건 아니에요. 지역 말은 '사투리'나 '방언'이라고 해서, 서울말과 대비해서 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the speech used in the Seoul area. The standard language is based on Seoul speech, but the two are not exactly identical. Regional speech is called '사투리' or '방언', and it is often contrasted with 서울말.

examples.ko: 선거철이 되면 길거리에 현수막이 가득 걸려요.
examples.en: When election season comes, banners fill the streets.
Every election season, candidates put forward new pledges.
During election season, candidates often visit the market.

examples.ko: 선거철이라서 뉴스에서 여론 조사 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: It's election season, so there's a lot of poll talk in the news.
The streets get noisy whenever election season arrives.

examples.ko: 선거철을 맞아 투표를 독려하는 광고가 많이 보여요.
examples.en: With election season here, you see many ads encouraging people to vote.

explain: '-철'은 어떤 일이 한창인 때를 말해서 '장마철, 휴가철, 단풍철'처럼 써요. '선거철'은 선거를 앞두고 분위기가 뜨거운 시기를 가볍게 말할 때 좋아요. 공식적으로는 '선거 기간'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '-철' marks a time when something is at its peak, as in '장마철', '휴가철' and '단풍철'. '선거철' is a casual way to talk about the heated period before an election. The official term is '선거 기간'.

examples.en: Customers have the right to choose their menu.

examples.ko: 직원들에게 근무 시간 선택권을 주는 회사가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More companies are giving employees a choice of working hours.

examples.ko: 학생도 수업을 고를 선택권이 있어야 해요.
examples.en: Students should also have a choice in picking their classes.

examples.ko: 물건을 살지 말지 선택권은 소비자에게 있어요.
examples.en: The choice of whether to buy something belongs to the consumer.

examples.ko: 선택권이 너무 많으면 오히려 고르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If there are too many options, it's actually hard to choose.

examples.ko: 내 삶의 선택권을 내가 갖고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to have the right to make choices about my own life.

explain: '선택'은 고르는 행동이고, '선택권'은 고를 수 있는 권리나 자유예요. '선택권이 있다, 선택권을 주다, 선택권이 없다'처럼 써요. 고를 방법이 없을 때는 '선택의 여지가 없다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '선택' is the act of choosing, while '선택권' is the right or freedom to choose. It is used as '선택권이 있다', '선택권을 주다' and '선택권이 없다'. When there is no way to choose, people also say '선택의 여지가 없다'.

examples.ko: 섬마을 아이들은 배를 타고 학교에 가요.
examples.en: Children in the island village go to school by boat.

examples.ko: 그 섬마을 사람들은 하나의 공동체처럼 살아가요.
examples.en: The people of that island village live like one community.

examples.ko: 방학 때 섬마을에 가서 낚시를 했어요.
examples.en: During vacation, I went to an island village and fished.
The island village is very quiet at night.
My grandmother lived her whole life in an island village.

examples.ko: 섬마을 주민들이 태풍 준비를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The residents of the island village are preparing for the typhoon.

explain: '섬'에 있는 작은 '마을'이에요. 도시가 아니라 시골 같은 조용한 분위기가 있어요. 바닷가 마을은 '어촌'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a small village on an island, with a quiet, rural feel rather than a city one. A seaside fishing village can also be called '어촌'.

examples.en: The raging waves crashed over the breakwater.
My little brother got angry because his toy was taken.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 성나 있어요? 누가 놀렸어요?
examples.en: Why are you so worked up? Did someone tease you?
The boss got angry and shouted.
He is the kind of person who goes quiet when he gets angry.

examples.ko: 성난 마음을 가라앉히고 천천히 이야기해 봐요.
examples.en: Calm your angry heart and let's talk it through slowly.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '화나다'가 더 자연스러워요. '성나다'는 '성난 파도, 성난 얼굴'처럼 꾸며 주는 말로 자주 보여요. 화를 겉으로 드러내는 것은 '화내다'라고 해요.
explain_en: In everyday talk, '화나다' sounds more natural. '성나다' often shows up as a modifier, as in '성난 파도' (raging waves) and '성난 얼굴' (an angry face). Showing your anger outwardly is '화내다'.

examples.en: I rent out the spare room and receive monthly rent.
The landlord rented out the upstairs.
I listed the shop with a realtor to rent it out.
If you rent out a house, it's easier to look after.
The room I put up for rent hasn't gone yet.
In this building, we rent out the first floor and live on the second.

explain: 집이나 가게를 빌려주고 돈을 받는 것을 말해요. '세를 놓다'라고 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 반대로 돈을 내고 빌려 사는 것은 '세(를) 들다, 세 들어 살다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is about lending out a house or shop and receiving money for it. It can also be written with a space as '세를 놓다'. The opposite, paying to live in someone else's place, is '세(를) 들다' or '세 들어 살다'.

examples.en: I filled the basin with water and washed my face.
The sink was clogged, so I called a plumber.
Please leave the toothbrush next to the washbasin.

examples.ko: 새 세면기는 높이가 낮아서 아이도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: The new washbasin is low, so even kids can use it.
Water keeps leaking from the bathroom washbasin.

examples.ko: 호텔 세면기에 머리카락이 있어서 직원에게 말했어요.
examples.en: There was hair in the hotel washbasin, so I told the staff.

explain: 욕실에서 얼굴과 손을 씻는 그릇 모양의 설비를 말해요. '세면대'라고도 해요. 설비 전체를 가리킬 때는 '세면대', 물을 받는 그릇 부분은 '세면기'로 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the bowl-shaped fixture in a bathroom for washing your face and hands. It is also called '세면대'. Some people use '세면대' for the whole fixture and '세면기' for the bowl that holds the water.

examples.en: The child rides a tricycle around the park.

examples.ko: 세발자전거는 바퀴가 세 개라서 넘어지지 않아요.
examples.en: A tricycle has three wheels, so it doesn't fall over.
My nephew happily rides his tricycle around the yard.
The tricycle broke, so I fixed the wheel.

examples.ko: 두발자전거를 배우기 전에 세발자전거에 먼저 앉아 봤어요.
examples.en: Before learning a two-wheeled bike, I first sat on a tricycle.

examples.ko: 세발자전거도 이제 작아져서 아이가 못 타요.
examples.en: The tricycle has become too small now, so the child can't ride it.

explain: 바퀴가 세 개인 어린이용 자전거예요. 짝이 되는 말은 '두발자전거'이고, 두발자전거를 처음 배울 때는 '보조 바퀴'를 달기도 해요. '세 발'과 붙여서 한 단어처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a children's bicycle with three wheels. Its counterpart is '두발자전거', and kids sometimes add '보조 바퀴' (training wheels) when first learning to ride one. It is written together as a single word.

examples.en: Things in life don't go the way I want.

examples.ko: 앞으로 어떻게 될지 세상일은 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: No one knows how things in life will turn out.

examples.ko: 요즘 아버지는 세상일에 별로 관심이 없으세요.
examples.en: These days my father isn't very interested in what's going on in the world.

examples.ko: 세상일을 다 알 수는 없어도 뉴스는 매일 봐요.
examples.en: I can't know everything that happens, but I watch the news every day.
When I'm upset about worldly matters, I go for a walk.
Life's affairs aren't that simple.

explain: 세상에서 벌어지는 여러 가지 일이나 살아가는 일을 두루 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 '세상사'는 글에서 더 많이 보여요. '세상일이 뜻대로 안 되다'처럼 인생이 마음 같지 않다는 말에 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It covers the many things that happen in the world and in living one's life. The similar '세상사' appears more in writing. It often fits remarks that life doesn't go as you wish, as in '세상일이 뜻대로 안 되다'.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to a car wash and cleaned my car.
This car wash is self-service, so it's cheap.

examples.ko: 세차장 앞에 차가 줄을 서 있어요.
examples.en: Cars are lined up in front of the car wash.

examples.ko: 비 오기 전에 세차장에서 세차하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't wash your car at the car wash right before it rains.

examples.ko: 집 근처에 새로 생긴 세차장이 깨끗해요.
examples.en: The newly opened car wash near my house is clean.
I opened a map app to find a car wash.

explain: 차를 씻는 곳이에요. 직접 씻는 곳은 '셀프 세차장', 기계가 자동으로 씻는 곳은 '자동 세차'라고도 말해요. 차를 씻는 일은 '세차하다', 손으로 직접 씻는 건 '손세차'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a place for washing cars. A place where you wash it yourself is a '셀프 세차장', and one with machines may be called '자동 세차'. Washing a car is '세차하다', and washing by hand is '손세차'.

examples.en: I prepared a short introduction before the presentation.

examples.ko: 책 앞부분에 작가의 소개말이 실려 있어요.
examples.en: The author's introductory words appear at the front of the book.
Keep your introduction short and clear.
I included my strengths in my introduction too.
I read the club's introduction and applied.

examples.ko: 프로필 소개말 칸에 뭘 쓸지 고민돼요.
examples.en: I'm wondering what to write in the profile bio box.

explain: 사람이나 모임, 책을 소개하려고 하는 말이나 쓴 글이에요. 글로 쓴 소개는 '소개글'이라고도 하고, 자신을 소개하는 건 '자기소개'라고 해요. 앞에 나서서 말할 때는 '소개말을 하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the words you say or write to introduce a person, group or book. A written introduction can also be called '소개글', and introducing yourself is '자기소개'. When speaking up front, you say '소개말을 하다'.

examples.en: I was born in the year of the ox and my brother in the year of the tiger.

examples.ko: 소띠 사람들은 성실하다는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: People born in the year of the ox often hear that they are diligent.
My mother was born in 1961, the year of the ox.

examples.ko: 올해 소띠 운세를 보고 싶어서 앱을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened an app because I wanted to check this year's fortune for the ox sign.

examples.ko: 친구랑 제가 둘 다 소띠인 걸 오늘 알았어요.
examples.en: I found out today that my friend and I are both ox-year people.
Please recommend a gift that suits someone born in the year of the ox.

explain: '띠'는 태어난 해를 열두 동물로 나타낸 거예요. 한국에서는 나이를 물을 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 묻기도 해요. 같은 띠끼리는 열두 살 차이가 나고, 이를 '띠동갑'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '띠' shows the year of your birth through one of twelve animals. In Korea, people sometimes ask '무슨 띠예요?' as a way of asking about age. People of the same animal are twelve years apart, which is called '띠동갑'.

examples.en: I joined a reading small group at work.
A small group has few people, so it's easy to talk.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 러닝 소모임이 매주 토요일에 모여요.
examples.en: The running group in our neighborhood meets every Saturday.

examples.ko: 소모임을 직접 만들고 싶은데 어떻게 하면 될까요?
examples.en: I want to start a small group myself; how should I do it?
This month's small group topic is movies.
My weekends are busy because of small group activities.

explain: 취미나 관심사가 같은 사람들이 모이는 작은 모임이에요. '동호회'는 조금 더 공식적이고 규모가 큰 느낌이고, '동아리'는 주로 학교에서 써요. 요즘은 앱에서 소모임을 찾는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: It is a small gathering of people with a shared hobby or interest. '동호회' feels more formal and larger, and '동아리' is mostly used at school. Many people now find small groups through apps.

examples.en: I took a hand mirror out of my bag and checked my hair.

examples.ko: 이 손거울은 작아서 가방에 쏙 들어가요.
examples.en: This hand mirror is small, so it fits right in a bag.
At the hair salon, they showed me the back of my hair with a hand mirror.
The hand mirror broke, so I have to buy a new one.
I always carry at least one hand mirror.
Sunlight is reflecting off the hand mirror on the desk.

explain: 손에 들거나 가지고 다닐 수 있는 작은 거울이에요. 벽에 걸거나 서서 전신을 비추는 거울은 '거울'이나 '전신거울'이라고 해요. '손'이 붙은 말은 '손수건, 손전등'처럼 들고 쓰는 물건을 자주 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is a small mirror you hold in your hand or carry around. Mirrors hung on walls or showing your whole body are '거울' or '전신거울'. Words with '손' often refer to things you hold and use, like '손수건' and '손전등'.

examples.en: The presenter explained with big hand gestures.
The hand movements were funny, so everyone laughed.
Sign language is a language spoken with hand movements.
The hand movements are too fast for me to follow.

examples.ko: 손동작 하나만 봐도 요리 실력이 느껴져요.
examples.en: You can feel someone's cooking skill from a single hand movement.

examples.ko: 노래에 맞춰 손동작도 같이 해 보세요.
examples.en: Try doing the hand movements along with the song.

explain: 손을 움직이는 모양이나 방법을 말해요. 누구를 부르거나 가리키는 손의 움직임은 '손짓'이라고 해요. 몸 전체를 쓰는 건 '몸짓'이라고 하고, 노래나 춤에 맞춘 손의 움직임은 '손동작'이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It refers to the shape or way the hands move. A hand movement for beckoning or pointing is called '손짓'. Using the whole body is '몸짓', and hand movements that go with a song or dance are naturally '손동작'.

examples.en: My knuckles are thick, so rings don't fit over them.

examples.ko: 손마디는 어릴 때 다쳐서 약간 휘었어요.
examples.en: My finger joint got hurt as a child and is slightly bent.

examples.ko: 일을 오래 했더니 손마디마다 굳은살이 박였어요.
examples.en: After working for a long time, I got calluses on every finger joint.
When you crack your knuckles, they make a sound.
Deep wrinkles are carved into Grandma's finger joints.
I put a bandage between the finger joints.

explain: 손가락이 꺾이는 마디 부분을 말해요. '손가락 마디'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. '마디'는 나무나 대나무의 마디에도 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means the joint parts where the fingers bend. People also spell it out as '손가락 마디'. '마디' is also the word used for the joints of trees and bamboo.

examples.en: In winter you stay warm if you sleep under a cotton comforter.

examples.ko: 할머니 집에 가면 두꺼운 솜이불이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a thick cotton comforter at Grandma's house.
Cotton comforters are hard to wash, so we air them in the sun.
I fell asleep right away after lying under the cotton comforter.
I crawled under the cotton comforter to warm up.
I wrapped the baby snugly in a cotton comforter.

explain: 안에 솜을 넣어 만든 이불이에요. 이불은 '덮다', 바닥에 까는 것은 '요'라고 해서 '요를 깔고 이불을 덮다'라고 말해요. 요즘은 솜 대신 오리털이나 극세사로 만든 이불도 많아요.
explain_en: It is a comforter filled with cotton batting. You 'cover yourself' with an 이불, while the one laid on the floor is a '요', so people say '요를 깔고 이불을 덮다'. Nowadays many comforters are made with down or microfiber instead of cotton.
